content.text:
We need to resolve a March order from Winterfell. The actionGuidance shows reachable regions from Winterfell: castle-black (land, no castle), flints-finger (land, castle=1), greywater-watch (land, no castle), karhold (land, no castle), moat-cailin (land, castle=1), the-stony-shore (land, no castle), white-harbor (land, castle=1). The reachable list includes also "the-stony-shore" and "white-harbor". The actionGuidance also says "canLeavePowerToken": false, meaning we cannot leave a control token when vacating Winterfell? Actually "canLeavePowerToken": false means we cannot leave a power token? The note says "No control token will be spent." So we will vacate Winterfell empty, but we have home area (Winterfell) which is automatically controlled, so we don't need a token. So we can move the unit(s) out.

We have units in Winterfell: from board: winterfell has a Stark knight (id 45). Also we have a ship in Bay of Ice (id 34) but that's not in Winterfell. So only one unit in Winterfell: a knight. Since an army is defined as 2+ units, a single unit is not an army, so supply constraints don't apply to moving a single unit. However, after moving, Winterfell will be empty, but as home area, we keep control.

We need to decide where to move the knight. Options: castle-black (no castle), flints-finger (castle=1, owned by Greyjoy), moat-cailin (castle=1, owned by Greyjoy), white-harbor (castle=1, neutral? Actually white-harbor is a land area with castle=1, currently no control token, no units). Also greywater-watch (no castle, owned by Greyjoy). karhold (our own area, no castle). the-stony-shore (no castle, neutral). We need to consider combat: moving into an area with enemy units triggers combat. Let's check each target's current units and control.

We need to use check_neighbours to see details of each reachable area. Let's query each.

{
  "area": "flints-finger"
}

Again neighbours. We need details of flints-finger itself. The tool returns neighbours of the area, not the area itself. But we can infer that flints-finger is a land area with castle=1, owned by Greyjoy? Actually from map: flints-finger [land; castle=1]: bay-of-ice, greywater-watch, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. So flints-finger is a castle area, currently controlled by Greyjoy? Let's check board for flints-finger. In board list, there is no entry for flints-finger, meaning no units, no control token. So control token? The control token is placed on areas controlled by a house. Since no token, it's neutral. So flints-finger is neutral (no control token). So moving into flints-finger would be moving into a neutral castle area with no enemy units, so no combat. We would capture it by moving a unit there, and we would gain control token automatically? Actually rule: When you move units into a neutral area, you take control of it (no token needed). So we would gain a castle area.

Similarly moat-cailin is a castle area (castle=1) owned by Greyjoy? Actually moat-cailin is a land area with castle=1, currently controlled by Greyjoy (controlPowerToken: "greyjoy"). So moving there would trigger combat because there are no units there (units list empty). But there is a control token. Does moving into an area with a control token but no units cause combat? No, combat only occurs if there are enemy units. Control token alone does not cause combat. So moving there would capture the area (replace control token). However, we need to check if there is a garrison? No garrison. So we can capture without combat.

White-harbor is a land area with castle=1, currently no control token (board list doesn't have white-harbor). So capture without combat.

Greywater-watch has enemy units (Greyjoy footman and knights). So moving there would cause combat. Also castle=0. So we could attack there.

Karhold is a land area with no castle, currently controlled by Stark (our own). So moving there would be moving within our own area, no combat, but we would vacate Winterfell and move to Karhold, leaving Winterfell empty but we keep control as home. That would not gain any new castle.

The-stony-shore is a land area with no castle, neutral. So moving there would capture a neutral area (no castle). Not beneficial for victory points.

Castle-black is a land area with no castle, currently controlled by Stark (our own). So moving there would be moving within our own area, no combat, no new castle.

Greywater-watch is enemy units, no castle, but could be attacked to gain a land area (but not a castle). Might be strategic to attack Greyjoy.

We need to consider supply: we have supply 1, which allows one army of size up to 2? Actually supply track: supply 1 permits army sizes: 3,2 (from table). Wait supply 1: Permitted army sizes: 3,2. That means we can have up to 2 armies: one of size up to 3, one of size up to 2. Currently we have a single knight in Winterfell (size 1 army). We also have a ship in Bay of Ice (size 1 army). So we have two armies of size 1 each, which is fine. Moving the knight to a new area will keep the same number of armies (still 2). So supply is fine.

Goal: increase castle count. Currently we have 1 castle area (Winterfell). We could capture flints-finger (castle) or moat-cailin (castle) or white-harbor (castle). All are reachable. Which is best? Flints-finger is adjacent to Winterfell via Bay of Ice? Actually reachable list includes flints-finger. It is a castle area, neutral. Moat-cailin is a castle area owned by Greyjoy, but no units. Capturing it would remove Greyjoy's control token. That might be beneficial to reduce Greyjoy's castle count (they have 4 castles). White-harbor is neutral castle. So any capture gives +1 castle.

We need to consider potential retaliation: moving into a Greyjoy-controlled area might provoke them. But we can capture without combat, just replace control token. That is allowed. However, we must ensure we are not violating any rule about moving into an area with a control token but no units: you can move there and take control, removing the token. Yes.

Thus best move: move the knight from Winterfell to Moat-cailin (castle) to capture a castle from Greyjoy, reducing their castle count and increasing ours. That also gives us a new castle area (Moat-cailin). However, we would vacate Winterfell, but as home area we keep control, so we still have Winterfell castle. So we would have 2 castle areas (Winterfell and Moat-cailin). That is good.

Alternatively, moving to Flints-finger also gives a castle, but it's neutral, not taking from opponent. Moat-cailin reduces opponent's castle count, which is more beneficial.

Check if Moat-cailin is reachable: Yes, reachable list includes moat-cailin. It is a castle area with castle=1, currently controlled by Greyjoy. No units. So moving there is legal.

Thus we should move the knight (unit id 45) from Winterfell to Moat-cailin.

We need to produce JSON with moves array containing one object with destination_region_id "moat-cailin". The moves array can have multiple groups, but maxItems 1? Actually schema: moves is array, maxItems 1. So we can only specify one destination group? The schema says moves is array of UnitMove objects, each with destination_region_id. It doesn't include unit IDs. So we just specify destination region. The system will assume we move all units from source? Actually the description: "Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source." But schema only includes destination_region_id, no unit IDs. Possibly the system expects each move group to be a destination region, and all units from source will move there? But we can split? The schema doesn't allow specifying which units. So maybe we can only move all units to one destination. Since we have only one unit, it's fine.

Thus moves: [{"destination_region_id":"moat-cailin"}].

We need to ensure we are not leaving a control token: canLeavePowerToken false, but we don't need token for Winterfell.

Thus final answer.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.

actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. You choose which remaining March area to resolve now. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
